findings.title: Flat-branch checks omit the literal target or use unbound constant-zero checks
findings.evidence: SymPy computes 0*integrate(s-t,(t,0,s)); it omits f0(t)=t and -(flat_f-s). Sage checks is_zero(SR(0)) for the flat initial value and is_zero(SR(0)-(s-s)) for the flat integral without constructing the target integral. These are emitted as flat-branch coverage despite the frozen no-constant-true-check rule.
findings.consequence: The source-bound SymPy/Sage PASS fields do not establish the requested literal flat-branch checks. Multiplication by zero masks the wrong SymPy integrand. The target theorem is not refuted; the exactly aligned Lean theorem independently compiles.
findings.reproduction: review/flat_branch_coverage_probe.py, pinned SymPy 1.14.0: encoded unscaled integral=s**2/2, specified unscaled integral=s**3/6; at s=1 these are 1/2 and 1/6. Both zero-weighted residuals are zero. This falsifies coverage, not the C01 theorem.
findings.minimal_fix: In both affected sources bind f0(s)=s, form the actual interval integral (s-t)*f0(t), compare 0*integral against f0(s)-s, and derive the initial value by substitution into f0. Preserve this evidence and replace only the affected checks. Parent runs unchanged frozen external validators and decides the source-bound repair closeout.
